subject.title: fix: keep LINE group allowlists scoped [AI]

question: Should LINE immediately remove the shipped explicit `allowFrom` fallback for group sender authorization, and what upgrade handling is required for installations that relied on it?
rationale: The strict scope matches the LINE docs and closes an authorization gap, but the fallback has shipped for multiple releases and removing it can silently disable existing group workflows; repository policy requires explicit maintainer ownership of that security-versus-compatibility choice.

options.title: Strict scope with upgrade handling
options.body: Remove the fallback, add an operator-visible doctor or startup diagnostic with safe migration guidance, and require real LINE proof for denied and explicitly allowed group senders.

options.title: Accept immediate fail-closed break
options.body: Merge the strict behavior with documentation only and explicitly accept that affected installations must discover and repair their configuration after group messages stop.

options.title: Retain the fallback
options.body: Preserve current behavior and close or narrow this PR until maintainers define a different LINE group authorization contract.

recommendation.title: Strict scope with upgrade handling
recommendation.body: Remove the fallback, add an operator-visible doctor or startup diagnostic with safe migration guidance, and require real LINE proof for denied and explicitly allowed group senders.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and refactored the shipped allowlist boundary now being changed.
